exec: A major Japanese carrier says traffic congestion on its switches disrupted 5G SA service nationwide; it found no sign of a cyberattack.
plain: Docomo customers on its newest 5G service in Japan had trouble calling, using data and texting on 16 November until service was fully restored that afternoon. Docomo says traffic overloaded its switches.

sources.name: NTT Docomo notice: 5G SA service recovered (16 November 2026)
NTT Docomo notice: sixth report, partial recovery (16 November 2026)

summary: NTT Docomo says customers subscribed to its 5G SA (Standalone) service nationwide had difficulty using voice calls, data and SMS from 10:02 to 15:58 on 16 November, when it confirmed full recovery. Docomo gives the cause as a concentration of traffic on the switches serving 5G SA customers and says its investigation found no sign of unauthorised access or a cyberattack. Other 5G and 4G users, MVNOs and emergency calls were not affected.
title: NTT Docomo 5G SA voice, data and SMS hard to use nationwide on 16 November

validation.note: NTT Docomo's own recovery notice and sixth report read (follow-up 22 Nov); replaces the MLQ.ai roundup, which had been read only as a search excerpt.
